claim: iXsystems (2024-05-29) moved TrueNAS Apps from k3s/Helm to Docker Compose in 24.10 because 'K3s and Helm charts have been too complex and less reliable' and 'Helm charts are powerful, but they are more complex and less portable'; the third-party TrueCharts Helm catalogue lost support

Docker docs: Docker Content Trust and the Notary v1 service at notary.docker.io are being fully retired; shutdown 2026-12-08 after brownouts in July and August 2026; alternatives named are Sigstore/Cosign and Notation
Universal Blue PR #3075 (merged 2026-11-07) 'retire standalone NVIDIA images' removes NVIDIA akmods image pins and build logic; comment: 'We don't need to maintain the world'

Eclipse Foundation (2025-09-23): Open VSX 'is enterprise-class infrastructure that requires significant investment in security, staffing, maintenance, and operations'; 'the current model of unlimited, no-cost use cannot continue indefinitely'; rate limiting introduced

systemd issue #32762 (opened 2024-05-11 on 256~rc1, still open; fix PR #32967 open): systemd-sysext must mount each image to read extension-release; 'If one image fails to mount, then no extension is merged' (crypt_activate_by_signed_key ENODEV unhandled); Poettering: should 'apply what we can, and skip but log'

projectbluefin/server #32 (2026-08-27, closed 2026-09-06): a k3s sysext versioned on the OS-release axis could not ship a k3s security patch without an OS point release, and every OS point release re-downloaded an unchanged extension; fixed by decoupling the version (commit 041ebb7)

The Register (2024-03-28): signed, strictly confined fake crypto-wallet snaps in the Snap Store cost one user ~9 BTC (~$490k); re-uploads came from new accounts; Canonical switched to manual review of all new snap name registrations

Flatcar issue #1576 (opened 2024-11-01, open): the official nvidia-driver sysext hides ZFS modules; modules.dep in the merged /usr/lib/modules/6.6.54-flatcar lists nvidia but not zfs; 'modprobe zfs' fails, insmod works

Flatcar issue #1448 (2024-05-17, open): maintainer guidance for custom kernel modules is a directory sysext with ID=_any; a docs maintainer notes the sysext 'still overrides modules.dep, so multiple sysexts may conflict' and a modprobe hook may be needed

flatcar/scripts PR #2976 'Fix depmod issues with sysext kmods' (merged 2025-08-12): when several kmod sysexts are active one sysext's depmod files win; fix removes depmod files from every kmod sysext and runs depmod in a temporary overlay via a modprobe hook on each activation; build-time modules.dep was rejected because module versions can differ
